name: plan-tooling-scoping-decisions
body:
Change-set apg-plan-phases-scoping — spec authored (tier 1-3 + spine).

WHAT: `apg_plan_phases` must report only the requirements the current project/branch is responsible for. The bug: `opencode-suite/tools/apg_plan_phases.ts` loads all `Requirement` nodes (line 41) and flags any without a `Satisfies` edge unsatisfied (line 82); a project's plan is transient and dies with the branch, so requirements delivered by other projects keep no surviving `Satisfies` and read unsatisfied forever (apg-cleanup: 24-25 of them).

DECIDED in-scope definition (the SPEC.md open question, settled with the user): in-scope = branch-added requirements ∪ requirements this project's phases Satisfy. Branch-added mirrors the binary's `solution_nodes_added_on_branch` (`rust.apg.plan_cmd.verify.solution_nodes_added_on_branch`, `src/plan_cmd/verify.rs` lines 240-287) — a layer node file present on this branch but absent from the default branch. The suite tool may shell out to git (the lib already runs subprocesses via `Bun.$`).

PRESERVED findings: no-tasks, done-but-under-review, Gates cycles. PROJECT-LOCAL findings: `unsatisfied` = in-scope requirements with no Satisfies from a phase of THIS project; `over-satisfied` = requirements Satisfied by more than one phase OF THIS project.

SPINE AUTHORED:
- requirement `requirements.requirement.plan-phases-project-scoping` (feature `plan-tooling`), contained by `requirements.user.graph-consumer`.
- domain `domain.group.plan-tooling` (supporting) ⊃ `domain.entity.plan-phases-tool` (kind entity) + `domain.value.project-requirement-scope`.
- `drives`: requirement -> group, entity, value.
- `realised-by`: group, entity, value -> `solution.container.opencode-suite`.
- `implemented-by`: `solution.container.opencode-suite` -> `opencode-suite/tools/apg_plan_phases.ts`, `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts`, `opencode-suite/lib/apg.test.ts`, `opencode-suite/tests/boundary.e2e.test.ts`.

JUDGMENT CALLS:
- No new solution component. The brief directs the `implemented-by` edges onto the existing anchor `solution.container.opencode-suite`, so a dedicated component would duplicate the same code claim; the container is the natural anchor and already contains the suite's components.
- `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` IS an implement target (resolving the brief's "if the helper lands here"): the branch-delta helper is single-sourced in the shared lib because the tool's top-level logic is a default-exported `tool({...})` (not unit-testable), while the lib is unit-tested by `apg.test.ts`. If the plan instead puts the helper in the tool file, this edge must be reconciled.
- `detectCycle` (`ts.apg-opencode-suite.tools.apg_plan_phases.detectCycle`) is deliberately NOT an `implemented-by` target: its behaviour (Gates cycles) is preserved.

CONSTRAINTS: `requirements.constraint.plan-tooling-change-boundary` (no binary change; suite-tool-only) attaches to the requirement; `solution.constraint.suite-is-product-source` (opencode-suite is `include_str!` product source; the repo's `.opencode/**` are never edited) attaches to the container. `global.constraint.no-real-project-test` is reused (not duplicated) to bound the e2e test to scratch `/tmp` repos.

KNOWN CONSEQUENCE: `opencode-suite/agents/plan-writer.md` (line 213) depends on `apg_plan_phases` reporting unsatisfied requirements for its self-review; this scoping makes that check project-local, which is the point. No agent-guidance change is required by this change-set.
